correctness.rationale: Finite-k strict log concavity follows from the beta-binomial atom at zero and mean yield > dormant survival. Uniform-subsample convex order proves strict optimal-reserve decrease. Conditional LLN plus first-order derivative signs classify the limiting optimizer; Beta inverse moment is finite exactly when alpha>1. For r<1, the finite optimum tends zero, and splitting its exact reciprocal first-order identity into K=0 and K>0 yields q_k/h_k -> 1-r by conditional Binomial reciprocal bounds and dominated convergence; q_k has the explicit Gamma-ratio equivalent. Special examples are exact; the standalone checker tests rational identities, not infinite proofs. All assumptions and critical unproved limits are explicitly separated.

originality.rationale: The distinctive claim is not the classical concave bet-hedging objective or its first-order condition. It is the beta-mixed spatial regime transition r=(s/B)E[P^-1] with a sharp polynomial dormant-reserve equivalent, together with a critical exact finite-k boundary. The 1987 directly relevant paper was materially read and its approximate lognormal correlated-yield formulation does not state or dominate this beta-binomial rare-event law. The inaccessible 1988 full text remains a named nonzero risk, as do unindexed equivalent formulations. Actual targeted semantic and literature searches found no stronger covering theorem; absence of hits is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: Spatial and temporal spreading of reproductive risk is a central biological allocation problem. The new result pinpoints how a common weather component changes the limit from zero dormancy to a persistent positive reserve, or produces a quantitatively sharp polynomial reserve with a coefficient determined by the weather low-tail exponent; a distinct exact critical law is exhibited. Beta mixing is a natural explicit exchangeable-overdispersion model. The phase distinction and coefficient can inform sensitivity analyses of habitat correlation and germination policy, without claiming empirical calibration or a general ecological intervention theorem.
